details.publicNotes:
The instruments in an animated orchestra are usually beautifully crafted from fine materials and adorned with intricate designs. When animated properly by a professional, they remain perfectly still and silent until commanded to perform, which they do flawlessly. However, the performances of animated orchestras are a popular topic of debate among music aficionados. Some admire their precise artistry, while others say they lack emotion or soul.

Under the guidance of their conductor, animated orchestras can also protect their performance halls from dangerous intruders. Regrettably, not all animated orchestras possess the same qualities. Depending on the skill of the practitioner who animates the orchestra, some instruments might behave erratically. A misbehaving maelstrom of violins, trombones, drums, flutes, and other instruments could overwhelm inexperienced crafters, playing random discordant snippets of music and attacking indiscriminately. Even properly made orchestras might develop these dangerous tendencies with a bit of precise sabotage, and when left to their own devices, such faulty animated orchestras first attack their conductor and numerous audience members.

Once all of the survivors have fled and the screams have died down, the abandoned orchestra will wander endlessly in search of a new audience, performing their deadly song for whoever they come across. Though an exceptionally skilled crafter might be able to restore an animated orchestra back to its original function, surviving the orchestra's onslaught long enough to repair it is a challenging task.

Tools of the Trade

Animated orchestras might be able to move and play themselves under their own power, but when they lie dormant, they can also be played like normal instruments. An orchestra might play a set of musical instruments every day without ever suspecting they are enchanted, until the instruments fly from their hands to fight a threat—or, if the orchestra is particularly incompetent, to punish the orchestra with violence.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 18/45/80 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning), armor (heavy), shield, perception item, skill items (Acrobatics, Performance)

Eligible Imbued Properties body, bane, constitution, dexterity, energy resistant (spirit, vitality, void), fortification, music, sensory (darkvision), sturdy, wild, winged

description.value: Like normal objects, an animated orchestra has Hardness. This Hardness reduces any damage the swarm takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated orchestra is reduced to fewer than half its Hit Points, or immediately upon being damaged by a critical hit, its construct armor breaks, removing the Hardness and reducing its Armor Class to 18.

Trigger The animated orchestra is targeted by an attack and can see the attacker

Effect Woodwind instruments play a quick and frenzied melody, creating a swirling barrier of sound. The animated orchestra gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

The animated orchestra's brass instruments resonate with power and let loose a thunderous blast of sound dealing @Damage[(3d10+5)[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] (@Check[fortitude|dc:19|basic] save). On a critical failure, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 minute. The animated orchestra can't use Brass again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Brass]]{1d4 rounds}.
The animated orchestra unleashes a thunderous barrage of percussive strikes against each creature in its space, dealing @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:19|basic] save).

The animated orchestra's stringed instruments hum with magic as they weave a slicing melody into the air. The melody crescendos into a ferocious symphony of supernatural blades, dealing @Damage[(2d6+5)[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:burst|distance:10] within 120 feet (@Check[reflex|dc:19|basic] save).
